provenance_note: The Palmer chick-production source and schema were previously probed on a failed validation branch, but no colony-size versus reproductive-output statistic or result was computed or opened. This contract freezes that new endpoint before execution.

source.title: Adelie penguin colony-specific chick production, 1991, present.

question: Within the same Palmer island and breeding season, do larger Adelie breeding groups produce chicks disproportionately faster than breeding-pair number, as predicted by a positive group-size effect on reproductive performance?

biological_hypothesis.name: size-dependent reproductive advantage
biological_hypothesis.null: Expected chick production is proportional to breeding-pair number within each island-season.
biological_hypothesis.alternative: Expected chick production scales superlinearly with breeding-pair number, consistent with higher chicks per pair in larger groups.
biological_hypothesis.mechanistic_scope: A superlinear effect would be consistent with social facilitation and/or reduced per-pair predation pressure in larger groups, but would not identify the causal mechanism by itself.

season_definition: For January chick-production censuses, season_start_year = calendar year(time) - 1.

eligibility.duplicate_rule: Fail closed if more than one usable row exists for the same island, colony_code and season_start_year.
eligibility.island_season_risk_set: At least 3 eligible colony codes, non-zero variance in log breeding-pair number, and total chicks > 0.

primary_model.family: conditional Poisson / multinomial allocation within island-season
primary_model.equation: E[chicks_i] proportional to pairs_i^beta within each island-season.
primary_model.conditioning: Condition on the observed total chick count C_s in each island-season, so p_i(beta) = pairs_i^beta / sum_j pairs_j^beta.
primary_model.reason: This avoids regressing chicks-per-pair on pair number, which would share a denominator and can create mathematical coupling.

effect_size.estimate: Common beta maximizing the summed conditional multinomial log-likelihood across eligible island-seasons.
effect_size.interpretation: beta = 1 means constant chicks per pair; beta > 1 means larger groups have higher per-pair reproductive output; beta < 1 means diminishing per-pair output with group size.

primary_inference.statistic: Conditional score U at beta = 1 summed across island-seasons.
primary_inference.null_simulation: Within each island-season, simulate chick counts from Multinomial(C_s, pairs_i / sum pairs) while holding pair counts and C_s fixed.
primary_inference.p_value: one-sided upper-tail Monte Carlo p with +1 correction

sensitivities.leave_one_island_out: Report beta_hat and score direction after removing each island in turn.
sensitivities.minimum_pairs_2: Repeat after excluding rows with only one breeding pair.
sensitivities.overdispersion_cv10: Exploratory Gamma-Poisson colony-level resampling around proportional means with CV=0.10.

diagnostics.adult_denominator_overlap: Where possible, compare the chick-dataset breeding-pair count with the November breeding census by island, colony and season; report exact-equality fraction.
diagnostics.ratio_descriptive_only: chicks_per_pair may be summarized for display but must not be the primary regression response.

interpretation_boundaries: A positive result supports size-dependent reproductive performance, not a specific predator or social mechanism.
A null or beta <= 1 result argues against using social facilitation as the explanation for the observed concentration/extinction ordering.
Do not infer causality from colony size if unmeasured terrain or snow exposure could jointly affect size and chick production.
Do not change the ratio-free primary model after seeing the result.
